record.paper_title: Towards Knowledge Exchange: State-of-the-Art and Open Problems
record.original_question: What knowledge-base mapping generation methods are needed for ontology-based data access, where heterogeneous relational sources are accessed through a target knowledge base as a virtual view, mapping rules must support efficient query rewriting, and the source and target models have different expressive power?

evidence.quote: Additional research is needed on KGMTs to support the unique requirements of OBDA [46].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the ontology-based data access (OBDA) setting, in which a collection of heterogeneous relational data sources is exposed as a virtual instance of a target knowledge base (ontology) via a set of mapping rules. A mapping rule associates a SQL (or relational-algebra) query over the source schema with a conjunctive pattern over the target ontology's vocabulary (concepts, roles, and attributes), so that query answering over the ontology can be reduced to query rewriting and unfolding into SQL over the sources.

Design a methodology (and accompanying algorithms) for automatically generating such knowledge-base mapping rules that simultaneously satisfies the following requirements:

1. Heterogeneity: The procedure must accept multiple relational sources with differing schemas, constraints, and naming conventions, and must produce a unified set of mappings against a single target ontology.

2. Expressiveness gap: The source schema (relational, typically expressible in a restricted first-order fragment with key/foreign-key constraints) and the target ontology (expressed in a description logic such as a member of the DL-Lite family or OWL 2 QL, supporting class/role hierarchies, inverses, and existential restrictions) have different expressive power. The generated mappings must bridge this gap correctly, i.e., the certain answers obtained by rewriting any conjunctive query over the ontology and unfolding through the mappings must coincide with the intended semantics of the integrated virtual knowledge base.

3. Efficient rewritability: The produced mapping rules must be of a syntactic form (e.g., GAV with bounded existential depth, or T-mappings) for which perfect rewriting of unions of conjunctive queries is guaranteed to terminate and produce SQL of polynomial size in practice, enabling efficient query answering on top of standard relational engines.

Provide such a mapping-generation method, prove its correctness and completeness with respect to a clearly specified semantics of the virtual knowledge base, and characterize the classes of source schemas and target ontologies for which it is guaranteed to produce mappings that admit efficient query rewriting.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature on OBDA continues to identify mapping generation under heterogeneous sources, expressiveness mismatch between relational schemas and description-logic ontologies, and guaranteeing efficient query rewriting as active and unresolved research challenges. Surveys on knowledge graph construction and ontology-mediated query answering describe these as ongoing problems with partial solutions (e.g., T-mappings, bootstrapping tools like BootOX, Mastro), but no comprehensive automated method satisfying all three requirements has been established.

status_evidence.title: Rewriting Approaches for Ontology-Mediated Query Answering
status_evidence.snippet: Novel rewriting approaches for several extensions of OBDA aimed at understanding their relative expressiveness and paving the way for efficient query answering algorithms.
status_evidence.claim: Efficient query rewriting in expressive OBDA settings is an ongoing research line.

status_evidence.title: OBDA Constraints for Effective Query Answering
status_evidence.snippet: Redundancies in generated SQL queries are detrimental to performance in complex industrial OBDA scenarios.
status_evidence.claim: Producing mappings that yield efficient SQL rewritings is still an open engineering and theoretical issue.

status_evidence.title: Engineering optimisations in query rewriting for OBDA
status_evidence.snippet: Optimized methods that produce queries with fewer unions have been proposed.
status_evidence.claim: Optimization of mapping-driven rewriting is an active research area without a definitive solution.
